topic: CompTIA A+ Core 2 (220-1202) exam preparation - operating systems, security, software troubleshooting, and operational procedures
exam_format: Maximum of 90 questions in 90 minutes, delivered at Pearson VUE test centers or online-proctored. Question types include multiple choice (single and multiple response), drag-and-drop, and performance-based questions (PBQs). Scored 100-900 with a passing score of 700 for Core 2. This is the current V15 exam (220-1202), which launched March 25, 2025 and replaced 220-1102, with an estimated retirement around 2028 - tell candidates to verify the current exam version and objectives on CompTIA's official site before scheduling. To earn the full CompTIA A+ certification a candidate must pass BOTH Core 1 (220-1201) and Core 2 (220-1202). Exam fee is approximately USD 259 per exam (varies by region and voucher; bundles exist) - present it as approximate and advise confirming current CompTIA pricing. The certification is valid for three years and can be renewed through CompTIA's continuing-education program.
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple response clearly marked 'Select TWO/THREE', plus scenario items modeled on the exam's performance-based tasks; every item is a practical support scenario asking which OS setting, security control, remediation step, or procedure is correct - NOT rote definitions
audience: Aspiring and early-career IT support and help-desk technicians, desktop support specialists, and field service technicians. CompTIA recommends about 9-12 months of hands-on experience, though no formal prerequisite is required. Core 2 completes the CompTIA A+ certification (with Core 1) and pairs naturally with the Network+ (N10-009) and Security+ (SY0-701) courses in this catalog as the first step of the CompTIA trifecta.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Operating Systems
domains.notes: Comparing Windows editions and features; using Windows tools and the command line (Task Manager, MMC/snap-ins, Control Panel and Settings applets, Disk Management, System Configuration, and commands such as ipconfig, ping, netstat, nslookup, chkdsk, sfc, gpupdate/gpresult, net use, robocopy); installing and configuring Windows (upgrade vs clean install, boot methods, partition/file systems NTFS/FAT32/exFAT, features); configuring networking on a client (IP settings, network shares, workgroup vs domain, VPN, proxy, firewall); and understanding macOS and Linux features/tools and basic commands. Choosing the correct OS tool, command, install method, or setting for a described scenario.

domains.name: Security
domains.notes: Summarizing security measures and their purposes (physical, logical, and device-hardening); comparing wireless security protocols (WPA2/WPA3, AES, RADIUS/TACACS+) and authentication methods (MFA, biometrics); detecting, removing, and preventing malware (types and tools, and the malware-removal best-practice steps); recognizing social-engineering attacks, threats, and vulnerabilities; configuring Windows security settings (users/groups, NTFS vs share permissions, UAC, BitLocker/EFS, Defender); securing SOHO networks and mobile/embedded devices; and applying data destruction/disposal and workstation/browser security best practices. Choosing the correct security control, authentication method, or remediation for a described scenario.

domains.name: Software Troubleshooting
domains.notes: Troubleshooting common Windows problems (boot/BSOD, slow performance, services not starting, profile issues, updates) and applying the correct fixes; troubleshooting and resolving PC/mobile OS and application issues; and - importantly - troubleshooting malware symptoms and applying the malware-removal best-practice steps IN ORDER (investigate/identify symptoms; quarantine the infected system; disable System Restore in Windows; remediate - update anti-malware and scan; schedule scans and run updates; re-enable System Restore and create a restore point; educate the end user). Choosing the correct troubleshooting step or most likely fix for a described symptom, emphasizing the malware-removal step ORDER.

domains.name: Operational Procedures
domains.notes: Applying best-practice documentation and support procedures (ticketing, asset/knowledge management, standard operating procedures, change management); implementing backup and recovery methods and account/data recovery; following safety procedures (ESD, electrical, personal safety) and environmental controls; understanding incident response, licensing/EULA/DRM, regulated data (PII, PCI, GDPR, PHI), and communication/professionalism; and using remote-access technologies and basic scripting concepts (file types .bat/.ps1/.sh/.py/.vbs/.js, use cases, and risks). Choosing the correct procedure, safety practice, documentation type, or communication approach for a described workplace scenario.

extra_guidance: CompTIA A+ Core 2 (220-1202) is the current V15 Core 2 exam (launched March 25, 2025, replacing 220-1102) and completes the CompTIA A+ certification together with Core 1 (220-1201). State clearly that BOTH exams are required for the A+ credential and that this course covers Core 2 only, with a companion Core 1 course available. The exam is scenario- and task-based, including performance-based questions (PBQs) - the real skill it tests is 'given this support/security situation, which OS setting, security control, remediation step, or procedure is correct,' NOT memorizing definitions. This is a vendor-neutral, READ-AND-UNDERSTAND course - show and explain real Windows tools, Control Panel/Settings paths, command-line examples (ipconfig, sfc, chkdsk, gpupdate, net use, etc.), permission models, and step-by-step procedures rather than requiring specific hardware. Cover the exam's signature emphases exactly: NTFS vs share permissions and permission precedence, UAC and standard vs administrator accounts, BitLocker vs EFS, WPA2 vs WPA3 and wireless auth, MFA and biometrics, the malware types and - most important - the SEVEN-STEP malware-removal best practice IN ORDER (identify symptoms; quarantine; disable System Restore; remediate/update+scan; schedule scans and updates; re-enable System Restore and create a restore point; educate the end user), the Windows command-line utilities and when to use each, file systems (NTFS/FAT32/exFAT), backup types and the 3-2-1 rule, ESD and electrical safety, regulated-data types (PII/PCI/GDPR/PHI), change-management and ticketing documentation, and scripting file types and their risks. Flag classic traps: NTFS vs share permission conflicts (most restrictive wins across share+NTFS; least restrictive within NTFS), 'disable System Restore before remediating and re-enable after,' WPA3 over WPA2, and 'educate the end user is the LAST malware-removal step.' Use current terminology and note technology evolves, so verify against CompTIA's current objectives. The four domain names and weights above are CompTIA's official 220-1202 exam-objective weights (Operating Systems 28%, Security 28%, Software Troubleshooting 23%, Operational Procedures 21%) - use them verbatim. NEVER promise a pass or use the word 'guarantee' in ANY form (Udemy compliance) - use 'exam-focused preparation' framing throughout, including learning objectives and who-this-is-for. Present the exam fee as approximate (~USD 259 per exam, varies by region; bundles exist) and note the 3-year validity with CompTIA continuing education. The final chapter must be a full exam simulation with a 90-minute, up-to-90-question time-management strategy that accounts for performance-based questions (PBQs). Scan the practice bank for stray other-vendor/cloud-specific terms before upload per the pipeline compliance rules.
